html:
SMTO-EXE-0141 — App control isn't installed or supported on that computer

GUID: 5420f664-9072-5d3f-9377-11be8a2923f1
Slug: ui-adapter-unavailable
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: ui

What happened

  • The Gateway on that computer doesn't have working app-control parts, either because they weren't installed correctly or its operating system isn't supported. SMTO didn't click or type anything.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask whoever manages the computer running the Gateway (the helper program SMTO uses on that computer) to run the Gateway installer again there and make sure it finishes without errors. This usually means the parts the Gateway needs to control apps are missing, and the installer adds them back.
  2. Once no tasks are using that Gateway, restart it. The Gateway only loads the repaired parts when it starts.
  3. In SMTO, open Settings › Setup › Gateways, select Check connection for that Gateway, then start a new task. Existing tasks keep the Gateway abilities they started with; a new task picks up the repaired ones.

What success looks like

  • Check connection shows that Gateway as connected, and a new task can read and use the app's buttons and fields.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the computer's operating system, to the person who manages that Gateway. Repair it in place: don't delete its pairing, saved sign-ins, settings, browser profiles or task files. Giving a Skill permission to control apps doesn't install the missing parts.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Gateway's native UI component could not be loaded because its platform dependencies are missing or the operating system is unsupported, so the safe unavailable fallback was used.

What this means

  • The platform adapter could not be constructed, lacked required dependencies or used the safe unsupported-platform fallback. Unknown UI error kinds also resolve to this fallback category. Only the existing explicit UI request may observe or mutate the selected desktop. Secure values stay redacted, stale references are not retargeted, and uncertain native input is not automatically repeated.

Why this can happen

  • The platform adapter could not be constructed, lacked required dependencies or used the safe unsupported-platform fallback. Unknown UI error kinds also resolve to this fallback category.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect platform and ui.status dependency/session facts; the fallback label alone does not identify which dependency failed.

How to fix it

  • Run ui.status and check the Gateway's platform. If the supported native UI dependencies (PyGObject/AT-SPI on Linux, PyObjC on macOS, comtypes on Windows) are missing, repair the Gateway in place by rerunning its supported installer on that host, then, after active work settles, restart it and refresh its metadata. Unsupported operating systems cannot use native UI; desktop session and permission problems have their own error codes. Unknown UI error kinds also map to this code.
  • Inspect ui.status and the Gateway platform. If its supported native adapter dependencies are missing, reinstall or repair the affected Gateway by rerunning its supported installer on that Gateway host. After installation succeeds and active work is settled, restart the Gateway and refresh its metadata. Unsupported operating systems and desktop permissions require their own remedy.
  • If installation repair is indicated: From the matching repository checkout, run ./install.sh for the server and local Gateway, or use the Gateway-only installer: ./src/gateway_agent/install.sh on Linux, ./src/gateway_macos/install.sh on macOS, or .\src\gateway_windows\install.ps1 on Windows. Run it as the account used by the Gateway so its environment and browser caches are repaired.
  • After an installation repair: After active jobs and uncertain operations are reconciled, restart the affected Gateway. Restart the server too if the shared installer updated it. Refresh Gateway metadata before starting a new task.
  • Confirm the reported capability works on the selected Gateway after correcting its diagnosed cause. If installation repair was needed, require the installer checks to pass. Refresh metadata and start a new task when capabilities change; existing tasks keep their captured snapshot.

Retry and execution caution

  • Confirm the reported capability works on the selected Gateway after correcting its diagnosed cause. If installation repair was needed, require the installer checks to pass. Refresh metadata and start a new task when capabilities change; existing tasks keep their captured snapshot. Inspect prior execution receipts before repeating work.

How to verify the fix

  • A supported installed adapter reports ready under the intended session and permissions.

What not to do

  • Do not replay uncertain mutations, read secure fields, record input or bypass OS permissions.
  • Repair the installation in place; do not delete Gateway pairing, credentials, settings, browser profiles or task artifacts.
  • Granting a Skill permission does not install its dependencies.

Technical notes

  • Only the existing explicit UI request may observe or mutate the selected desktop. Secure values stay redacted, stale references are not retargeted, and uncertain native input is not automatically repeated.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
